name: Non-syndromic Bicoronal and Sagittal Craniosynostosis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Non-syndromic Craniosynostosis

criteria.description: Presence of abnormal skull shape consistent with bicoronal and sagittal suture fusion
CT or MRI evidence of premature fusion of bicoronal and sagittal sutures without other suture involvement
No clinical or genetic evidence of syndromic craniosynostosis (e.g., no limb anomalies, no midface hypoplasia typical of syndromes)
Normal neurodevelopmental milestones in early infancy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical skull deformity with radiological confirmation of bicoronal and sagittal suture fusion and exclusion of syndromic features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may be performed to exclude syndromic causes but is not diagnostic for non-syndromic forms.

pathognomonic.notes: Leads to brachycephaly and abnormal forehead contour
searchTerms: early fusion of coronal skull sutures
premature joining of top side skull bones
early skull bone fusion at coronal suture

pathognomonic.notes: Results in scaphocephaly with elongated skull shape
searchTerms: early fusion of sagittal skull suture
premature joining of midline skull bones
early skull bone fusion at sagittal suture

pathognomonic.symptomName: Abnormal skull shape with combined brachycephaly and scaphocephaly features
pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic cranial deformity due to dual suture involvement
searchTerms: unusual skull shape with mixed short and long features
combined short and elongated head shape
skull deformity with brachycephaly and scaphocephaly traits

common.notes: May include irritability, vomiting, or bulging fontanelle
searchTerms: headache and vomiting from brain swelling

common.notes: Mild delays may be observed in some cases
Prominent forehead due to bicoronal synostosis

occasional.notes: Misalignment of the eyes due to orbital deformities
Conductive hearing loss secondary to cranial base abnormalities
Obstructive sleep apnea due to midface hypoplasia
Rare but possible due to increased intracranial pressure

rare.notes: Accumulation of cerebrospinal fluid due to impaired drainage
Due to optic nerve compression or orbital abnormalities
Severe cases may show intellectual disability

imaging: CT scan showing premature fusion of bicoronal and sagittal sutures
3D reconstruction of skull demonstrating abnormal cranial shape
genetic: Absence of mutations in syndromic craniosynostosis genes (e.g., FGFR2, TWIST1) in most cases
other: Physical examination revealing characteristic cranial deformities

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of limb anomalies, midface hypoplasia, and genetic mutations
Multiple suture involvement with systemic features
Asymmetric skull shape due to external molding forces

redFlags: Signs of increased intracranial pressure (e.g., vomiting, bulging fontanelle)
references: Cohen MM Jr. Craniosynostosis: Diagnosis, Evaluation, and Management. 3rd ed. Oxford University Press; 2000.
